title: Exactly-once, as it is
dek: A Kafka transaction is two logs agreeing after the fact: a decision in one, markers in others, a stall in between. This last part of a five-part teardown reads Apache Kafka 4.4.0 and takes one apart byte by byte: the coordinator's state machine, Transaction Version 2, a 78-byte marker, the last stable offset that stalls plain records too, the epoch fence, and KAFKA-20734, known upstream, where a marker for an offline partition is dropped and the coordinator says complete. That bug has no tagged fix as of 6 November 2026. The part ends where exactly-once ends, and with the whole collection's findings register.
byline: 6 November 2026 · Subject: kafka@1156b275 (Apache Kafka 4.4.0) · Part 5 of 5 · Read from the source; measured where this machine allows
description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 5: the transaction coordinator, TV2, control markers on disk, the last stable offset, epoch fencing, hanging transactions and KAFKA-20734, what exactly-once does not cover, and the collection's findings register.
og_description: Part 5 of a five-part Kafka teardown at kafka 1156b275 (4.4.0): commitTransaction returning means decided, not visible; one open transaction stalls plain records too; and KAFKA-20734, known upstream and untagged as of 6 November 2026, hides committed records from read_committed while the bytes stay.

badges_callout:
How to read the badges

from the code marks a fact read from the pinned source, cited as repo/path:line: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 (1156b275), franz-go main (123ec885), librdkafka v2.16.0 (c6c9973c). Paths are relative to the kafka/ checkout unless a repo is named; core/…/txn/ abbreviates core/src/main/scala/kafka/coordinator/transaction/. A bare file name is under a tree named nearby. measured here marks output from small clusters on loopback, on a shared 2-vCPU machine with one disk and no iptables. Timings show relative behaviour, never capacity. Each scenario is a single run unless it says otherwise. librdkafka was read, never run, and trunk was read, never built. Faults here are process kills and SIGSTOP; no real power cut was run. reconstruction marks a judgement drawn from those sources rather than read in one place. Register ids such as D10 point at the findings register below.

This is Part 5 of 5 of Kafka, taken apart. Part 1 reads the log on disk; Part 2 follows one request on the wire and through the broker; Part 3 reads replication and the metadata quorum; Part 4 covers producers and consumer groups.

sections.title: Two logs, one transaction
sections.brief: A transaction is a decision in one log and markers in others; commitTransaction returning means decided, not visible. transactions:F1-F21, F34-F40, F117-F119, X48.

sections.title: Transaction Version 2
sections.brief: TV2, default since 4.0, bumps the epoch per transaction and drops client RPCs; franz-go runs it, and librdkafka does not. transactions:F22-F33, F67-F70, F150, F153, X56, X57.

sections.title: Markers on disk
sections.brief: A marker is a one-record control batch; an abort also writes .txnindex, and offsets show permanent gaps. transactions:F43-F50, F113-F116, F147-F149, TR-transactions-1..4.

sections.title: The last stable offset
sections.brief: One open transaction stalls every record behind it, including plain ones, and endOffsets hides it; the client does the filtering. transactions:F51-F63, F120-F122, F143-F145, X53-X55, TR-transactions-5.

sections.title: Fencing and a dead coordinator
sections.brief: The epoch is the fence, and a coordinator crash keeps the decision, provided the data partition has a leader when the successor sends the marker. transactions:F64-F66, F71-F82, F123-F129, F137, F138, X51, TR-transactions-7.

sections.title: Hanging, and KAFKA-20734
sections.brief: A partition can hold a transaction the coordinator has forgotten; KAFKA-20734 is a known route in that broke atomicity at RF 3 with all replicas down. Fixed upstream, no tagged fix as of 6 November 2026. transactions:F41, F42, F83-F97, F130-F136, F139-F142, F154-F158, X49, X50, X52, TR-transactions-6, TR-transactions-8, TR-verify-d-rf3, TR-verify-d-pause.

sections.title: What exactly-once does not cover
sections.brief: The guarantee is read-process-write within Kafka; everything outside needs its own cooperation. transactions:F98-F112, F146, F151, F152.

sections.title: Findings register
sections.brief: All of §4 as a compact HTML table figure, every row keeping its D-number and an anchor: class, claim, upstream status, part. Prose held to the target; table words counted separately. Nothing reported upstream; never 'we discovered'.
